card: This pull request encapsulates HTTP request parsing state by removing HTTPRequest::SetState(), making per-section parsing methods private, and introducing a single HTTPRequest::Load() method that advances internal state automatically. It resolves an encapsulation leak highlighted during review of PR 35829, where external callers could still manipulate the request state enum. Additionally, HTTPRemoteClient::ReadRequest() is flattened into an internal member method. There are no behavioral changes or prerequisites.
evidence: PR description links to review discussion on PR #35829 (discussion_r3860447518) noting that SetState() leaves the internal state machine exposed to external callers
problem: After PR 35829 made request fields private, external callers with a reference to an HTTPRequest could still arbitrarily mutate its state enum via SetState(). In addition, callers had to coordinate multiple sequential parsing methods manually.

risk.why: A parsing or state machine regression in HTTP server request handling could cause RPC or REST requests to hang, fail parsing, or disconnect clients.

scope_notes: Internal refactor of HTTP server request parsing accompanied by mechanical updates to unit tests and the http_request fuzz harness.
summary: Encapsulates HTTP request state transitions by removing HTTPRequest::SetState() and making individual LoadControlData, LoadHeaders, and LoadBody parsing methods private. Callers instead invoke a single HTTPRequest::Load() method that advances the internal state machine. Request parsing in HTTPRemoteClient is also simplified by flattening ReadRequest() into a private TryReadRequestInternal() member function.
